findings.title: retryCount cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
findings.body: File packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts line 39: the deleteMany OR second branch is { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } with no method filter, while the first branch is scoped to method SMS. As written any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) with retryCount > 1 will be deleted, even though retryCount is only maintained by this SMS cron. This causes unintended data loss for other channels; the condition should also require method SMS (and likely scheduled:false).

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries
findings.body: File packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts line 184 (repeated line 195): retry is recorded as data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } using the value read earlier in findMany. If the cron overlaps or two instances run concurrently, both read the same value and write the same incremented value, losing one retry and delaying deletion forever. Use atomic data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } instead.

findings.title: Missing message/sendTo path never increments retryCount
findings.body: File packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts line 158: retryCount is only incremented inside if (message?.length && sendTo) else-branch or on thrown exception. When sendTo is missing (e.g. no smsReminderNumber) or message is empty, the loop does nothing and leaves the reminder with scheduled:false and unchanged retryCount. That reminder will be refetched on every cron run until scheduledDate, defeating the PR goal of stopping infinite retries for invalid/missing numbers; it needs an else that increments or deletes.
